cohort: The study included 81 premature infants (<34 weeks of gestational age), consisting of 40 ROP cases and 41 well-matched non-ROP controls.
finding: Higher blood levels of malonyl carnitine (C3DC) and glycine were statistically significantly different between ROP and non-ROP infants and are suggested as promising biomarkers to predict the occurrence of ROP.
cross-section timing: Metabolites were measured during the neonatal period for early diagnosis of ROP.
birth_weight: ROP cases: 1.263 ± 0.345 kg; Non-ROP controls: 1.220 ± 0.293 kg
gest_age: Overall: <34 weeks; ROP cases: 31.20 ± 4.62 weeks; Non-ROP controls: 30.96 ± 4.17 weeks
